faqs.question: What should be on a Halloween bucket list?
faqs.answer: Mix small, dated items across the whole season rather than stacking them on 31 October: something for the equinox, a full-moon walk, a leaf drive, a few home projects and one ticketed outing. Our list has 40 original items from 1 September to 5 November, each tagged solo, couple, family or friends with an estimated time and cost.

faqs.question: When should I start a Halloween bucket list?
faqs.answer: Start on 1 September, or at least by the equinox on 22 or 23 September. Last-minute planning is the norm: in our Raksha Bandhan 2026 data, a different festival with only 89 pages, 49.4% of greeting pages were built on the day itself.

faqs.question: How many things should I put on a Halloween bucket list?
faqs.answer: Pick 8 to 12 items you genuinely want to do and keep the rest as a menu. A 2026 study of UK household data found that dreading a loss weighs more than looking forward to an equal gain, so a huge unticked list can feel like a chore.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a fall bucket list and a Halloween bucket list?
faqs.answer: A fall bucket list covers the season without costumes or spooky themes, built around leaf colour, harvest food and cooler weather. A Halloween bucket list adds the holiday itself and usually ends on 31 October; ours runs on to Bonfire Night on 5 November.

faqs.question: When do the clocks go back around Halloween in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: UK clocks go back on the last Sunday in October: 25 October 2026 and 31 October 2027, which is Halloween night itself. US clocks go back on the first Sunday of November: 1 November 2026 and 7 November 2027.

faqs.question: Is there a full moon on Halloween in 2026 or 2027?
faqs.answer: No. In 2026 the October full moon is on 26 October, and Halloween falls a day before the last-quarter moon. In 2027 the October full moon is on 15 October and the new moon on 29 October, so Halloween night is nearly moonless.

faqs.question: When do fall leaves peak?
faqs.answer: It depends on latitude and elevation. The USDA Forest Service puts Colorado's White River aspens at gold in late September and Virginia's highland maples and oaks in mid to late October, so check a local foliage report the week before you drive.

faqs.question: What can I do on a Halloween bucket list by myself?
faqs.answer: Eleven of our 40 items are solo, from a weekly sunset log to reading Dracula on the dates its entries are written. Most take between 1 minute and 1 hour and cost $0 to $15 by our estimate.

faqs.question: How much does a Halloween bucket list cost?
faqs.answer: Most items on our list are estimated at $0, and family items stay at $6 or less each. The priciest is a costume fun run, at an estimated $20 to $40 entry, so a full season can stay cheap if you skip ticketed events.

faqs.question: How do I include someone far away in my Halloween bucket list?
faqs.answer: Post them something physical, like a pressed leaf from your drive, or send a personalised page. The regular Halloween card takes about five minutes with up to six photos, while the premium page adds a 60-second voice note and an unlock time.

article.contentMarkdown:
# A Halloween Bucket List That Runs From 1 September to 5 November

A Halloween bucket list works best as a season, not a single night: 40 small items spread from 1 September to Bonfire Night on 5 November, each with an estimated time and cost, so nothing piles up in the final week. That pile-up is real. When we measured Raksha Bandhan 2026 on our own platform (a different festival, and a small sample of 89 pages), 49.4% of greeting pages were built on the festival day itself, and not one was started more than 7 days ahead.

Below are 40 original ideas in five date windows, tagged by who they suit. You also get the 2026 and 2027 anchor dates and a short fall bucket list.

## What is a Halloween bucket list, and why start in September?

A Halloween bucket list is a written set of seasonal things to do before Halloween ends, ticked off one by one. Spread over 66 days instead of one weekend, it turns October into something to look forward to rather than cram.

That looking forward matters. In a 2026 randomised trial, [76 older adults completed a three-week online savouring programme](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13332415) whose six activities included picturing good events due in the coming days or weeks. The savouring group improved more consistently, with lower negative feelings and depressive symptoms a month later, though most group differences were not significant.

## Halloween season dates for 2026 and 2027

Moon and equinox times, in Universal Time (UT), come from the [US Naval Observatory's data service](https://aa.usno.navy.mil/data/MoonPhases). Clock changes follow UK and US rules:

- **September equinox:** 23 September 2026 at 00:05 UT (8:05 pm on 22 September in New York); 23 September 2027 at 06:02 UT.
- **Full moons:** 26 September and 26 October 2026; 15 September and 15 October 2027.
- **New moons:** 10 October 2026; 29 October 2027.
- **UK clocks go back:** 25 October 2026 and 31 October 2027, because the [Summer Time Order 2002](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2002/262/made) ends summer time on October's last Sunday.
- **US clocks go back:** 1 November 2026 and 7 November 2027, as [NIST notes daylight saving time ends](https://www.nist.gov/pml/time-and-frequency-division/popular-links/daylight-saving-time-dst) on November's first Sunday.
- **Halloween to Bonfire Night:** Saturday 31 October to Thursday 5 November 2026; Sunday to Friday in 2027.

Two quirks are worth planning around. In 2027 the UK clocks go back on Halloween night itself, giving it 25 hours, and that Halloween is nearly moonless, two days after the new moon.

## The Halloween bucket list: 40 ideas by date window

Each item lists who it suits, then our estimated time and cost in US dollars.

### 1. 1–21 September: late-summer warm-ups

- **1. Sunset log** (solo · 2 min a week · $0): note each Sunday's sunset and watch evenings shrink.
- **2. House-ghost biography** (family · 20 min · $0): name your home's ghost and its favourite room.
- **3. Last-light picnic** (couple · 2 h · $15–25): one outdoor dinner before the equinox, ending at sunset.
- **4. Tulip-bulb promise** (solo · 45 min · $10–15): plant bulbs, one wish each, checked in spring.
- **5. One-trick magician** (solo · 15 min a day · $0): learn one coin vanish for trick-or-treaters.
- **6. Lock the big outing** (friends · 15 min · $0): one poll, one date, one deposit by 21 September.
- **7. Costume clear-out** (family · 1 h · $0): donate outgrown costumes.
- **8. Dracula on its own dates** (solo · 10 min a day · $0 via a library): Bram Stoker's 1897 novel is told in dated entries, so read each on its day.

### 2. 22 September–4 October: equinox fortnight

- **9. Equinox shadow mark** (family · 10 min, twice · $0): chalk a stick's midday shadow at the equinox and on 31 October; north of the equator it grows.
- **10. Equal-halves dinner** (couple · 90 min · $20–30): pale food on half the plate, dark on the other.
- **11. September full-moon walk** (friends · 90 min · $0): on a route you know by daylight.
- **12. Pear or apple butter** (couple · 4 h, mostly simmering · $8–12): one jar kept, one given.
- **13. Charity-shop costume duel** (couple · 90 min · $10 each): buy each other's costume, no vetoes.
- **14. Coat-pocket notes** (couple · 20 min · $0): a hidden line in each winter coat.
- **15. First-frost bet** (friends · 5 min · $0): everyone names a date; the loser hosts in November.
- **16. House-sound recording** (family · 30 min · $0): slowed-down house creaks, played at the door.

### 3. 5–18 October: dark skies and peak leaves

- **17. Two-pumpkin race** (family · 5 min · $3–6): one mini pumpkin indoors, one outside; bet which softens first.
- **18. Dark-sky night** (friends · 2 h · fuel only): leave the streetlights behind at the new moon.
- **19. Leaf-peeping drive** (couple · half a day · fuel plus $5): timed to your local peak.
- **20. Pressed-leaf letter** (solo · 30 min · $1–2 postage): post the drive's best leaf to someone far away.
- **21. Seven-night monster doodles** (solo · 1 min a night · $0): no erasing; the best goes on the door.
- **22. Town-legend hour** (family · 1 h · $0): ask the library's local history desk for one town legend.
- **23. Five-apple blind tasting** (friends · 45 min · $10–15): numbered slices, one ranking each.
- **24. Organ-riff challenge** (solo · 20 min a day · $0): learn the opening of the Toccata and Fugue in D minor on a keyboard app.

### 4. 19–30 October: the run-in

- **25. The gifted hour** (solo · 1 h · $0): decide now what the UK's spare clock-change hour is for.
- **26. Full-moon porch supper** (couple · 1 h · $10–20): 26 October 2026; in 2027, move it to 15 October.
- **27. Painting tableau** (friends · 2 h · $0–10): restage Henry Fuseli's 1781 *The Nightmare* as a group photo.
- **28. Costume fun run** (friends · 2 h · $20–40 entry): a charity run, as one group character.
- **29. Leaf-pile long jump** (family · 30 min · $0): rake one pile and measure every jump.
- **30. T-shirt treat bag** (family · 30 min · $0): cut the sleeves off an outgrown T-shirt and knot the hem.
- **31. Photo-booth strip** (couple · 20 min · $5–10): four frames in autumn knitwear, to compare next year.
- **32. Guess-the-weight pumpkin** (friends · 10 min · $5–10): the closest guess chooses dinner.

### 5. 31 October–5 November: Halloween to Bonfire Night

- **33. Pumpkin bird feeder** (family · 30 min · $3 in seed): a halved, unpainted pumpkin filled with seed.
- **34. Clock-change sunrise breakfast** (couple · 1 h · $10): once US clocks go back, sunrise comes an hour earlier.
- **35. Neighbour thank-you note** (family · 15 min · $0): on 1 November, thank the best-decorated house.
- **36. Tick and keep three** (solo · 10 min · $0): copy three favourites into next year's diary.
- **37. Organised fireworks display** (friends · 2 h · $5–15): for Bonfire Night, safer than back-garden fireworks.
- **38. Compost the jack-o'-lantern** (family · 15 min · $0): chop it into the compost or garden-waste bin.
- **39. Leaf-mould bag** (solo · 15 min · $0–2): raked leaves in a holed bin bag become mulch.
- **40. The Dracula finale** (solo · 20 min · $0): the novel's last dated entry is 6 November.

## Which items suit solo, couples, families and friends?

The table counts the 40 items by who they suit, with the ranges they span.

| Who | Items | Est. time per item | Est. cost per item | Start with |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Solo | 11 | 1 min to 1 h | $0–15 | #8, Dracula |
| Couple | 9 | 20 min to half a day | $0–30 | #10, equal-halves dinner |
| Family | 11 | 5 min to 1 h | $0–6 | #2, house-ghost biography |
| Friends | 9 | 5 min to 2 h | $0–40 | #6, lock the big outing |

Families get the cheapest list ($6 or less per item); friends carry the ticketed costs.

## Fall bucket list: when do the leaves actually peak?

A fall bucket list is the same idea without costumes, and its one fixed date is your local leaf peak. The [USDA Forest Service fall colours guide](https://www.fs.usda.gov/visit/fall-colors), updated 18 September 2026, puts Colorado's White River aspens at gold in late September and Virginia's highland maples and oaks in mid to late October.

Peak shifts with latitude and elevation, so check a local foliage report first. The ten fall-only picks are items 3, 4, 12, 14, 15, 19, 20, 23, 29 and 39.

## Send one item to someone you cannot do it with

Some items belong to a person far away, like the pressed-leaf letter. Our pages are opened on a phone 48.3% of the time, and 90.9% of pages people start are finished and shared.

The [interactive Halloween card with photos and music](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes about five minutes, carries up to six photos and has them carve your chosen word into a pumpkin. The [premium Halloween page with a voice note and unlock time](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) takes about ten minutes, carries 12 photos and a 60-second voice note, and waits behind a countdown until your chosen moment.

To turn an item into a real plan, the [date invitation they must answer](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation) becomes a countdown after a yes. It suits item 26, the full-moon porch supper, best.

## When a Halloween bucket list is the wrong idea

A list can turn from something to look forward to into something to dread. A [2026 study of UK household panel data](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12818390), drawing on about 10,000 and later 40,000-plus households, found that dreading a future loss weighs more than looking forward to an equal gain. Forty unticked boxes can read as forty small losses, so choose 8 to 12 and treat the rest as a menu.

Skip the list in a season of grief, or for anyone Halloween frightens. SubhSandesh is the wrong tool for most items, too: our pages are English-only, made for one recipient and cannot replace the walk itself.

## Sources

- Pancini et al., *Applied Psychology: Health and Well-Being*, 4 July 2026.
- Dawson and Johnson, *Cognitive Science*, 20 January 2026.
- US Naval Observatory, Moon Phases and Earth Seasons data (undated).
- The Summer Time Order 2002 (SI 2002/262), made 12 February 2002.
- NIST, "Daylight Saving Time (DST)", created 2 March 2010.
- USDA Forest Service, "Fall Colors", updated 18 September 2026.

sources.stat: Pancini, Cremaschi, Degani, Cisotto & Villani, 'Savor-Aging' RCT, Applied Psychology: Health and Well-Being 2026 (CC BY): 76 healthy older adults (M = 69.9), 3-week online programme of six savoring activities across past/present/future, one being 'anticipation of positive events' (visualise positive events in the next hours, days or weeks). Savoring group showed more consistent improvements, with reductions in negative affect and depressive symptoms maintained at 1-month follow-up; most time x group interactions were not significant. Full text read.

Dawson & Johnson, Cognitive Science 50(1):e70160 (CC BY): using British Household Panel Survey (~10,000 UK households) and Understanding Society (40,000+ households) data, the displeasure of anticipating future losses outweighs the pleasure of anticipating equal gains; lab studies find little savoring but substantial dread. Full text read.

US Naval Observatory Astronomical Applications data (moon phases API queried 2026-10-14): full moons 26 Sep 2026 16:49 UT, 26 Oct 2026 04:12 UT, 15 Sep 2027 23:03 UT, 15 Oct 2027 13:47 UT; new moons 10 Oct 2026, 29 Oct 2027 13:36 UT; last quarter 1 Nov 2026 20:28 UT. The same service's Earth Seasons data: September equinox 23 Sep 2026 00:05 UT, 23 Sep 2027 06:02 UT.
The Summer Time Order 2002, art. 2: summer time ends 'at one o'clock, Greenwich mean time, in the morning of the last Sunday in October' (25 Oct 2026; 31 Oct 2027).
NIST: US daylight saving time 'ends at 2:00 a.m. on the first Sunday of November' (1 Nov 2026; 7 Nov 2027).

USDA Forest Service 'Fall Colors' (modified 18 Sep 2026): White River National Forest, Colorado, aspens 'turn brilliant gold in late September'; George Washington & Jefferson National Forests, Virginia, maples, poplars and oaks 'light up the highlands in mid to late October'.

structuralLimitations: No Halloween first-party data exists; first-party lines are platform-wide (phone share, publish rate) plus the Raksha Bandhan lead-time lines, disclosed in the body as a different festival with n = 89.

SERP: 1 WebSearch (US index) returned 9 results, 7 weak (small mom/craft blogs x6 URLs, processon.io spam); only Hallmark Ideas is a strong domain. thistinybluehouse.com returned 403 — judged from snippet only.
timeanddate.com returned 403 (bot wall, not worked around); clock-change dates are sourced to the Summer Time Order 2002 (UK) and NIST (US) and computed for 2026/2027. gov.uk is at its batch cap.
Equinox times come from the USNO Earth Seasons data; to keep outbound links at 6, the body links the USNO Moon Phases page for both, and the sources entry records both datasets.
Bram Stoker's Dracula (1897) is named but not linked: Project Gutenberg #345 text was checked — entries are dated from '3 May. Bistritz' through September and October to 6 November.

Savouring evidence is from older adults (Pancini 2026, n = 76) and most between-group effects were not significant; the body says so. Dawson & Johnson measure anticipation of income gains and losses, applied here by analogy to an unticked list.
All item times and costs are editorial estimates in US dollars, labelled as such in the body.
